fields.label: Status
fields.description: Written by the job with db.set_value, which skips validate() — the transition table in the controller is the backstop for desk and console edits, not the enforcement point.

fields.label: Subject
fields.description: Who the export is ABOUT, when it is about a person. Optional: 'everything said about the Henderson contract' is a legitimate request with no subject.

fields.label: Rooms
fields.description: Comma-separated room names. Frozen once requested — the manifest names what was exported, so editing the scope afterwards would make the manifest describe a different bundle.

fields.label: Include Deleted Message Bodies
fields.description: Decision D-9. OFF by default. When off, a deleted message appears in messages.jsonl as a tombstone and its text is in revisions.jsonl. Turning it on is recorded in the export_requested audit row.

fields.label: Reason
fields.description: Refused below 12 characters, and refused if it is a placeholder. Graded by chat.governance.access_report.reason_quality, the same grader the compliance report uses.

fields.label: Reason Category
fields.options:
HR or personnel matter
Legal, regulatory or compliance
Security investigation
Safety or site incident
Customer or contract dispute
Requested by the employee
Technical maintenance
Other
fields.description: What the subject may be shown, per decision D-3. Never the free text above.

fields.label: Bundle
fields.description: A private File attached to THIS request. Chat Export Request ships zero DocPerm, and Frappe's private-file check delegates to the attached document's has_permission — so /private/files/ is closed to everyone but Administrator and the only way to the bytes is the audited download endpoint.

fields.label: Downloads
fields.description: Every download also writes its own export_downloaded audit row; this is the cheap counter, not the record.
